LLM provider integrations implementing `ApiProvider` interface to call different AI services.\n4. \n5. ## Architecture\n6. \n7. Each provider:\n8. \n9. - Implements `ApiProvider` interface (`src/types/providers.ts`)\n10. - Transforms prompts → provider-specific API format\n11. - Returns normalized `ProviderResponse`\n12. - Handles auth, rate limits, retries, streaming\n13. \n14. ## Provider Lifecycle & Cleanup\n15. \n16. The evaluator (`src/evaluator.ts`) manages provider lifecycle. After evaluation completes, it calls `providerRegistry.shutdownAll()` to clean up resources.\n17. \n18. **If your provider allocates resources** (Python workers, connections, child processes):\n19. \n20. - Implement a `cleanup()` method on your provider\n21. - Register with `providerRegistry` for automatic cleanup\n22. - Resources are released in the evaluator's `finally` block\n23. \n24. **Reference implementations:**\n25. \n26. - `openai.ts` - Most comprehensive\n27. - `anthropic/index.ts` - Complex provider with subdirectory\n28. - `http.ts` - Generic HTTP pattern\n29. \n30. ## Logging\n31. \n32. See `src/providers/quiverai.ts` for a minimal example or `src/providers/openrouter.ts` for a more complex one.\n37. \n38. **Config priority:** Explicit options > Environment variables > Provider defaults\n39. \n40. ## Provider Routing\n41. \n42. Prefix dispatch in `src/providers/registry.ts` is case-sensitive and meaningful. Similar\n43. prefixes can route to different classes. When you add a new sub-type (e.g.\n44. `:moderation`, `:embedding`, `:realtime`) to one prefix, do one of:\n45. \n46. - Add the sub-type to every prefix it should work under, **or**\n47. - Explicitly fail-fast (throw with a clear message) for the prefixes that should not\n48.   support it.\n49. \n50. Silently mapping `foo:newtype` to a class that only handles `foo:chat` is a routing\n51. regression. Add a test in `test/providers/registry.test.ts` that asserts each\n52. prefix/sub-type pair resolves to the expected class or throws.\n53. \n54. ## Cache Key Hygiene\n55. \n56. Promptfoo's disk cache lives at `${getConfigDirectoryPath()}/cache` (typically\n57. `~/.promptfoo/cache`), unless overridden with `PROMPTFOO_CACHE_PATH` or\n58. `PROMPTFOO_CONFIG_DIR`. If an implementation stores literal cache-key strings, those\n59. strings persist to disk; if it stores hashed keys, the hash persists.\n60. \n61. - **Never include secrets in cache keys.** Strip `Authorization`, bearer tokens, API\n62.   keys, tenant tokens, signed metadata, and custom auth headers before building or\n63.   hashing a key. If those values materially change the response, use a non-secret\n64.   tenant/account identifier, a cache namespace, or disable caching for that path; do not\n65.   hash raw secrets into long-lived cache keys.\n66. - **Canonicalize before hashing.** `JSON.stringify({a, b})` and `JSON.stringify({b, a})`\n67.   produce different strings but represent the same config, so naïve stringification\n68.   causes cache misses for semantically identical requests. Sort keys (or use a\n69.   canonical-JSON helper) before hashing.\n70. - Reference pattern for stable key structure and canonicalized hashing:\n71.   `getModerationCacheKey` in `src/providers/azure/moderation.ts`.\n72. \n73. ## Caching Best Practices\n74. \n75. When implementing caching in your provider, **ALWAYS set the `cached: true` flag** when returning a cached response:\n76. \n77. ```typescript\n78. // ✅ CORRECT - Always set cached flag\n79. if (cachedResponse) {\n80.   const parsed = JSON.parse(cachedResponse as string);\n81.   return { ...parsed, cached: true };\n82. }\n83. \n84. // ❌ WRONG - Missing cached flag\n85. if (cachedResponse) {\n86.   return JSON.parse(cachedResponse as string);\n87. }\n88. ```\n89. \n90. **Why this matters:**\n91. \n92. - The `cached` flag allows downstream code to skip rate limiting delays\n93. - Performance metrics can distinguish between fresh API calls and cache hits\n94. - Evaluations can accurately track which responses were served from cache\n95. \n96. **Response type compatibility:**\n97. \n98. - `ProviderResponse` has `cached?: boolean`\n99. - `ProviderEmbeddingResponse` has `cached?: boolean`\n100. - `ProviderModerationResponse` has `cached?: boolean`\n101. \n102. **Reference implementations:**\n103. \n104. - `bedrock/converse.ts:985` - Sets cached flag correctly\n105. - `pythonCompletion.ts:194` - Example with spread operator\n106. - `google/vertex.ts:268` - Multiple cache points handled correctly\n107. \n108. ## Testing Requirements\n109. \n110. **CRITICAL: Tests must NEVER make real API calls.** Mock all HTTP requests.\n111. \n112. Every provider needs tests in `test/providers/`:\n113. \n114. - Mock API responses using `vi.mock`\n115. - Test success AND error cases\n116. - Test rate limits, timeouts, invalid configs\n117. - Run with: `npx vitest run test/providers/my-provider`\n118. \n119. ## Adding a Provider\n120. \n121. **All seven items are required** before a provider is complete:\n122. \n123. 1. Add tests in `test/providers/`\n127. 5. Add docs in `site/docs/providers/<provider>.md`\n128. 6. Add entry to `site/docs/providers/index.md` table (alphabetical order)\n129. 7. When testing async functions that internally use timers, you cannot simply `await` them—the promise will hang because fake timers don't advance automatically. Use this pattern:\n340. \n341. ```typescript\n342. it('handles async retry with delay', async () => {\n343.   // 1. Start the promise (don't await yet)\n344.   const promise = myAsyncFunctionWithRetry();\n345. \n346.   // 2. Run all timers to completion\n347.   await vi.runAllTimersAsync();\n348. \n349.   // 3. Real timers cause flaky tests because:\n359. \n360. - **Timer resolution varies**: Windows has ~15ms minimum resolution vs ~1-4ms on Linux/Mac\n361. - **Race conditions**: Code checking `Date.now()` multiple times can see different values if a millisecond boundary is crossed\n362. - **CI variability**: Tests may pass locally but fail under CI load\n363. \n364. **Anti-pattern** (causes flaky tests):\n365. \n366. ```typescript\n367. // ❌ AVOID: Real timers with small delays\n368. it('retries after delay', async () => {\n369.   const result = await functionThatRetries({ retryAfterMs: 1 }); // May timeout randomly\n370. });\n371. ```\n372. \n373. **Correct pattern**:\n374. \n375. ```typescript\n376. // ✓ CORRECT: Fake timers with controlled advancement\n377. it('retries after delay', async () => {\n378.   vi.useFakeTimers();\n379.   const promise = functionThatRetries({ retryAfterMs: 1000 });\n380.   await vi.runAllTimersAsync();\n381.   const result = await promise;\n382.   vi.useRealTimers();\n383. });\n384. ```\n385. \n386. ## Best Practices\n387. \n388. - Ensure all tests are independent and can run in any order\n389. - Clean up any test data or mocks after each test\n390. - Run the full test suite before committing changes\n391. - Test failures should be deterministic\n392. - For database tests, use in-memory instances or proper test fixtures\n393. - **Use fake timers** for any code involving `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, or timing-sensitive logic\n394. block\n const initialState = useMyStore.getState();\n \n describe('MyComponent', () => {\n   beforeEach(() => {\n     // Reset store to initial state before each test\n     act(() => {\n       useMyStore.setState(initialState);\n     });\n   });\n \n   afterEach(() => {\n     // Clean up after each test\n     act(() => {\n       useMyStore.setState(initialState);\n     });\n   });\n \n   test('user interaction updates store correctly', async () => {\n     const user = userEvent.setup();\n \n     // Verify initial state\n     expect(useMyStore.getState().items).toHaveLength(0);\n \n expect(useMyStore.getState().items).toHaveLength(1);\n     });\n   });\n });\n ```\n \n ### Key Patterns\n \n 1. **Capture initial state outside describe**: `const initialState = useMyStore.getState();`\n 2. **Reset in beforeEach AND afterEach**: Ensures test isolation\n 3. **Wrap setState in act()**: Required for React state batching\n 4. **Assert on getState()**: Verify actual store state, not that a mock was called\n 5. **Use waitFor for async**: Store updates may be asynchronous\n 6. **Mock external dependencies only**: Mock APIs, analytics, child components—NOT the store\n \n ### Anti-Pattern: Mocking the Store (avoid this)\n \n ```typescript\n // ❌ AVOID: Mocking the store hook loses integration coverage\n vi.mock('./useMyStore');\n const mockUpdateItems = They test `dist/src/main.js` directly using `spawnSync`.\n \n ```bash\n # Run smoke tests\n npm run test:smoke\n \n # Run specific smoke test file\n npx vitest run test/smoke/cli.test.ts --config vitest.smoke.config.ts\n ```\n \n **Location:** `test/smoke/` with fixtures in `test/smoke/fixtures/configs/`\n \n **Reference pattern** (from `test/smoke/filters-and-flags.test.ts`):\n \n ```typescript\n import { spawnSync } from 'child_process';\n import * as fs from 'fs';\n import * as path from 'path';\n import { afterAll, beforeAll, describe, expect, it } from 'vitest';\n \n const CLI_PATH = path.resolve(__dirname, '../../dist/src/main.js');\n const FIXTURES_DIR = path.resolve(__dirname, 'fixtures/configs');\n const OUTPUT_DIR = path.resolve(__dirname, '.temp-output');\n \n function runCli(args: string[], options: { cwd?: string } = {}) {\n   const result = spawnSync('node', [CLI_PATH, ...args], {\n     cwd: options.cwd || path.resolve(__dirname, '../..'),\n     encoding: 'utf-8',\n     env: { ...process.env, NO_COLOR: '1' },\n     timeout: 60000,\n   });\n   return {\n     stdout: result.stdout || '',\n     stderr: result.stderr || '',\n     exitCode: result.status ?? 1,\n   };\n }\n \n describe('My Smoke Tests', () => {\n   beforeAll(() => {\n     if (!fs.existsSync(CLI_PATH)) {\n       throw new Error(`Built CLI not found. Test the **built package** (`dist/src/main.js`), not source code\n - Use `spawnSync` with `node` to run the CLI directly\n - Fixtures go in `test/smoke/fixtures/configs/` (committed to git)\n - Temp output directories cleaned up in `afterAll`\n - `test/scheduler/slotQueue.test.ts` - Comprehensive fake timer usage\n - `test/scheduler/providerRateLimitState.test.ts` - Async code with timers\n \n ### Basic Pattern\n \n ```typescript\n import { afterEach, beforeEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from 'vitest';\n \n describe('MyTimerCode', () => {\n   beforeEach(() => {\n     vi.useFakeTimers();\n   });\n \n   afterEach(() => {\n     vi.useRealTimers();\n   });\n \n   it('handles timeout', () => {\n     const callback = vi.fn();\n     setTimeout(callback, 1000);\n \n     vi.advanceTimersByTime(1000);\n \n     expect(callback).toHaveBeenCalled();\n   });\n });\n ```\n \n ### Async Code with Timers\n \n When testing async functions that internally use timers, you cannot simply `await` them—the promise will hang because fake timers don't advance automatically. Use this pattern:\n \n ```typescript\n it('handles async retry with delay', async () => {\n   // 1. Start the promise (don't await yet)\n   const promise = myAsyncFunctionWithRetry();\n \n   // 2. Run all timers to completion\n   await vi.runAllTimersAsync();\n \n   // 3. Now await the result\n   const result = await promise;\n \n   expect(result).toBe('success');\n });\n ```\n \n ### Why Fake Timers Matter\n \n Real timers cause flaky tests because:\n \n - **Timer resolution varies**: Windows has ~15ms minimum resolution vs ~1-4ms on Linux/Mac\n - **Race conditions**: Code checking `Date.now()` multiple times can see different values if a millisecond boundary is crossed\n - **CI variability**: Tests may pass locally but fail under CI load\n \n **Anti-pattern** (causes flaky tests):\n \n ```typescript\n // ❌ AVOID: Real timers with small delays\n it('retries after delay', async () => {\n   const result = await functionThatRetries({ retryAfterMs: 1 }); // May timeout randomly\n });\n ```\n \n **Correct pattern**:\n \n ```typescript\n // ✓ CORRECT: Fake timers with controlled advancement\n it('retries after delay', async () => {\n   vi.useFakeTimers();\n   const promise = functionThatRetries({ retryAfterMs: 1000 });\n   await vi.runAllTimersAsync();\n   const result = await promise;\n   vi.useRealTimers();\n });\n ```\n \n ## Best Practices\n \n - Ensure all tests are independent and can run in any order\n - Clean up any test data or mocks after each test\n - Run the full test suite before committing changes\n - Test failures should be deterministic\n - For database tests, use in-memory instances or proper test fixtures\n - **Use fake timers** for any code involving `setTimeout`, `setInterval`, or timing-sensitive logic\n \n"},"toolTelemetry":{"properties":{"command":"view","options":"{\"truncateBasedOn\":\"tokenCount\",\"truncateStyle\":\"middle\"}","inputs":"[\"path\",\"command\"]","resolvedPathAgainstCwd":"false","fileExtension":"[\".md\"]","viewType":"file"},"metrics":{"resultLength":13678,"resultForLlmLength":13678,"responseTokenLimit":230500},"restrictedProperties":{}}},"id":"9ee043da-442c-4de8-825e-f660f580fe78","timestamp":"2026-06-01T14:19:39.216Z","parentId":"a9e1a530-13e3-44bc-a373-9ba335ad49c2"}
